articleTitle: Evaluating the Performance of Measurements Systems Using Data Processing Methods Based on Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this scientific paper, the manually and automated acquired data from vibrating-wire transducers will be analyzed. The forementioned sensors were mounted and managed by the authors’ research group during different national grants obtained over time. In most cases, when you first visually analyze the two data sets, manual and automated measurements, a strong discrepancy can be viewed. The manual data present a high dispersion due to the random errors introduced by the manual measurement instrument. To reveal the monitored phenomenon, displacement in this case, there is a need for a rigorous analysis which will validate at least one of the methods and finally will find the error source for the other one by imposing a correlation algorithm. To evaluate the performance of the installed automated data acquiring system, a Kalman filter was used for the large data series. The strong resemblance between the rough automated data obtained and the refined Kalman filter data set proves that the implemented system is accurate.

articleTitle: Noise Measurement System Based on Cross-Correlation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: High precision electronic applications require low noise devices in order to increase the resolution and stability of measurement equipment. All resistors generate thermal noise and low frequency noise that is highly dependent on the technology used to manufacture these components and the current flowing through them. This paper presents a low noise measurement system, based on cross-correlation method. The noise measurement system was applied for metal film resistors. Using cross-correlation, the noise introduced by the amplifiers is reduced significantly. The noise spectra were measured at room temperature in a frequency range from 0.5 Hz to 10 kHz. The results show that the equivalent input voltage noise of the system is 2 nV/√Hz at 1 Hz and 0.53 nV/√Hz for frequencies above 100 Hz. The resistor noise components, thermal and low frequency noise were identified by measuring the voltage spectral density for different bias voltages. The obtained data validated the system`s effectiveness.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Migration Resistance of Gold Surface Finishes
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: So far, only a few studies have been focused on the electrochemical migration (ECM) of gold or gold surface finishes of printed circuit boards. Therefore, this work focused on the evaluation and comparison of electroless nickel immersion gold (ENIG) and galvanic gold in terms of ECM. The copper surface was also included in the experiment as a reference value. The water drop test (WDT) was conducted with distilled water on the comb pattern electrodes with three different applied voltages, and time to failure (TTF) was measured. Energy Dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis of the dendrites was subsequently performed regarding their composition. The results showed an apparent difference in ECM behavior between the gold surface finishes. ENIG surface finish is more resistant to ECM than galvanic gold. Bare copper is the most susceptible to ECM among tested surface finishes. The difference in susceptibility to ECM among gold surface finishes is caused by their structure and how they cover the copper electrodes.

articleTitle: Distributed System Using Synthetic Data of Lithium-ion Battery Digital Twin for Battery Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The solution proposed presents the process methodology of creating a data set with measurements that simulate data obtained in factories during testing phases for battery industry. This set of synthetically generated data aims to model multiple batteries, some of which having different degradation conditions, by means of a digital twin of the battery. The created application generates this data from simulation, and it can be used in the generic infrastructure. MATLAB and Simulink were used for the design and generation of Lithium-ion battery models, simulating the variations in current and voltage within a battery during testing. All generated data is collected and sent into the cloud, into NI SystemLink™ Enterprise, for further analysis and processes using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning approaches.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of a Novel Printed Circuit Board Interconnection Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this study, we present a novel printed circuit board (PCB) interconnection technology known as KlettWelding, offering a promising solution for connecting PCBs, resembling board-to-board connectors. This joining process is significantly more energy-efficient than traditional methods such as sintering and soldering, as it operates at room temperature. Furthermore, this approach eliminates the need for organic additives commonly found in sintering and soldering pastes. Copper (Cu) serves as the preferred conductive material in PCBs, facilitating the realization of stacked PCBs connections through Cu/Cu bonding with KlettWelding at room temperature. This study highlights the achieved connections, emphasizing both their potential and the challenges they presented. We investigate and discuss the obtained measurement results concerning connection quality and electrical properties. The measurements were conducted based on the four-point probe method, utilizing a well-established measurement setup, across a temperature range from 10°C to 70°C. Additionally, we compared the obtained results with those of similar interconnections fabricated through reflow soldering.

articleTitle: Influence of Reflow Temperature Profile on the Intermetallic Layers Thickness at Different Surface Finishes
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: It is well known that the reflow temperature profile has an influence on the thickness of intermetallic layers. The higher the thermal treatment, especially above the melting temperature of solder alloy, the higher the thickness of intermetallic layers. The heating factor (time-temperature integral of temperature profile above the melting temperature) is commonly used for comparison of the heat treatment. This paper deals with a comparison of three different reflow temperature profiles (with three different heating factors: 242, 1061 and 1652 s.K), three surface finishes (Organic Solderability Preservative - OSP, Hot Air Solder Leveling – HASL and Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold – ENIG) of copper soldering pads and two solder pastes with the same composition of solder alloy (Sn96,5/Ag3,0/Cu0,5) but with different flux type (less aggressive - ROL0 and more aggressive - ROL1). The cross-sections of the samples were prepared after the reflow soldering process, followed by analysis by scanning electron microscope and measurement of intermetallic layers thicknesses. Results confirmed that the heating factor significantly influences the intermetallic layers. The highest thickness of intermetallic layers was achieved with the highest value of the heating factor. The surface finish HASL had the highest values of intermetallic layer thicknesses from all used surface finishes, whereas ENIG had the lowest. The higher values of intermetallic layer thickness were observed for the solder paste with a more aggressive flux, ROL1, than for ROL0.

articleTitle: Effect of TiO2 Nanoparticles Addition on the Electrochemical Migration of Lead-Free Sn-Bi Alloys
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This research aimed to investigate the susceptibility of Sn-58Bi alloys to Electrochemical Migration (ECM) when combined with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles tested in various solutions, including deionized water (DI), 1 mM Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, 500 mM Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, 1 mM NaCl, and 500 mM NaCl, using water drop (WD) test. The results revealed a heightened ECM susceptibility in Sn-58Bi alloys with the addition of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles, indicating an adverse impact of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticle incorporation. Furthermore, scanning electron microscopy and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) were utilized to analyze the surface morphology and elemental composition of dendrites formed after the WD tests. The outcomes showed the presence of dendrites and precipitates in both Sn-58Bi and Sn-58Bi-0.1% TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> cases. Sn was identified as the primary element in the dendrites, while Bi was not detected in the dendrites in any of the cases. Consequently, the reliability of electronics may be compromised when using Bi-Sn paste doped with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles, particularly in terms of ECM. Nonetheless, these nanoparticles could enhance other properties associated with modified microstructure, such as mechanical or thermal properties, which warrant further investigation.

articleTitle: Hydrogen in Automotive: LCA Study
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive cradle-to-gate Life Cycle Assessment of fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs), providing a comparative assessment against alternative and fossil fuel-driven counterparts. The research focuses on hydrogen as a fuel source, emphasizing two key production methods: natural gas reforming and water electrolysis. The scope of the study is set to the Czech Republic environment. Diverse sources of electric generation, such as wind and photovoltaics, are considered to supply the electrolysis process. The energy source mix predictions are set to year 2030 up to 2050. The feasibility of transitioning towards greater utilization of renewable energy sources within the context of privately owned vehicles is investigated in this work. Specifically, the study examines the exact part of the vehicle life cycle, starting with production to the use phase, with a consideration of the car’s lifetime, aiming to provide a nuanced understanding of their environmental footprint and clear comparability with each other. This study highlights the significant potential for reducing the environmental impacts of personal vehicles through the usage of hydrogen. With FCEVs emitting zero direct emissions, the total environmental impact is directly tied to the process of fuel production. Producing hydrogen through electrolysis, particularly when powered by photovoltaic or wind energy can significantly lower its emissions, especially in terms of greenhouse gas emissions.

articleTitle: Modeling the Optical Response of a Periodic Nanoparticle Arrangement with the Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The refractive index sensitivity of plasmonic sensors is in the focus of many recent investigations. The performance of these optical sensors heavily depends on the geometrical properties of the used nanoparticle arrangements and also the properties of the used illumination conditions, namely the incidence angle and polarization of the incident electromagnetic field. All of these parameters should be optimized in order to maximize sensor performance. This paper aims to design a computational model in Comsol Multiphysics’s Wave Optics module to investigate the effects of light incidence angle and polarization with finite element method on the sensitivity of a plasmonic sensor based on hegaxonally-arranged gold nanoparticles. The purpose of this paper is also to provide a guideline for the modeling of periodic nanoparticle arrangements with different excitation conditions.

articleTitle: Sustainability in Electronics - Testing Sensors with Polycarbonate Housing (PC) vs Poly Lactic Acid Housing (PLA)
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper presents the results of an experiment in which we used two temperature and vibration sensors identical to the technical parameters and in one of them we changed the polycarbonate case with a case printed on a 3D printer with a biodegradable material made of poly lactic acid. After the tests the results were very close and considering that PLA is a biodegradable material that is made from renewable resources such as corn starch or sugar cane and is cheaper than polycarbonate it turns out that this is the best solution for making vibration and temperature sensor housings.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Migration: Evaluating the Effect of Fe2O3 Nanoparticle Incorporation on the Reliability of SAC Alloys
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The effect of incorporating Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanoparticles on the reliability of SAC305 solder alloy from the perspective of electrochemical migration (ECM) behavior was investigated through water drop (WD) tests conducted in a 0.1 M NaCl solution under a bias voltage of 10 VDC. The reliability analysis of the WD test findings unveiled that the lifetime outcomes for the examined alloys conform to a well-defined two-parameter Weibull distribution. The addition of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanoparticles at varying weight percentages (0.1%, 0.25%, and 0.5%) to SAC305, denoted as nanocomposite SAC305-x(0.1, 0.25, 0.5 wt.% Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), led to a lower mean time to failure (MTTF) compared to pure SAC305. This outcome suggests a disadvantageous effect of incorporating Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanoparticles into SAC305 in terms of ECM performance. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed a dendritic morphology characterized by straight and perpendicular branching (fishbone-like) in the nanocomposite solder alloys while energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) identified Sn as the predominant element in the dendrites, indicating that the ECM characteristics of nanocomposite solders are still primarily driven by the dissolution of Sn.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion Cell and Battery Testing by Spectral Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper examines the possibility of testing a Lithium-Ion battery health and analyzing the reliability of energy storage system, by using a spectral analysis.

articleTitle: Soil Degradation of Sustainable PLA/Flax Substrates and Printed Circuit Board Assemblies
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this study, flax-fiber reinforced, flame-retarded polylactic acid (PLA) composite printed circuit board substrate samples were prepared to investigate the long-term effects of soil degradation on stability and structural changes. After a moderate heat stressing in reflow environment (170°C, 300 s), 16-16 pieces of substrates and blinking circuit boards were placed to a composting bin. The ongoing examinations started nine months ago. The weight changes of samples are registered regularly, along with control parameters of soil, namely the moisture content (%), conductivity (µS/cm) and temperature (°C) values with a sensor node. During the evaluation, weather conditions were also considered (daily and weekly values of average temperatures and rainfall amount). As the weather conditions influenced the moisture content and the temperature of the soil, moisture absorption and soil deposition expressed in a divided weight gain tendency, referring to the different seasons during the 31-week period.

articleTitle: How Different Cleaning Procedures Affect Reliability of Conductive Joints on E-Textiles?
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This article deals with the influence of different cleaning procedures (washing 40 °C, 60 °C, 92 °C, dry cleaning, wet cleaning) on reliability of conductive joints onto conductive stretchable textile ribbons. In the experiment, the two different conductive connection techniques (low temperature soldering, non-conductive adhesive glueing) are used. The results show that low temperature washing (40 °C) or wet cleaning can be used for cleaning of textiles with ribbons with acceptable degradation of joints electrical resistance. The results also show that higher temperature washing and dry cleaning significantly degrade joints electrical resistance and also the ribbon itself.

articleTitle: 3D printing conductive pastes based on polystyrene/graphite composite
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The objective of this work was to modify a commercially available 3D printer with a syringe extrusion system inspired by clay 3D printing systems and, afterward, to print conductive test samples from prepared pastes. The pastes were prepared by dissolving polystyrene insulation foam in acetone and adding electrically conductive graphite powder in various loadings. The pastes were homogenized by ultrasonication. Subsequently, the test samples were printed and rested overnight for evaporation of the acetone solvent. Cuboid samples were used for the measurement of the sheet resistance and volume resistivity, followed by analyses of thermal properties and microscopy. The samples containing 23 wt.% and 33 wt.% of graphite exhibited a significantly increased electrical conductivity. Benefiting from a simple preparation, these materials, in conjunction with modified syringe-based 3D printing, can be used in many applications where electrical conductivity is required, such as electromagnetic shielding or sensors.

articleTitle: Evaluation of semipermeable membranes for encapsulating gas sensors in human intestinal environments
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This work describes a comparison of biocompatible membranes to encapsulate gas sensors in the human intestinal tract. The goal is to identify semipermeable materials that allow intestinal gases to pass through the membrane while also separating them from other intestinal contents. Important aspects of this study are the membranes’ chemical resistance to gastric acid and their gas permeability. Chemical resistance was assessed by submerging selected membranes in artificial gastric acid. Surface structure of membrane samples before and after the acid treatment was compared using scanning electron microscopy and signs of degradation were documented. To characterize the membranes in terms of their gas permeability, an experimental setup was developed to measure average airflow through the membranes. A constant pressure of 7 kPa was applied across the membrane and flow rate Q of air was measured over a predefined surface area A. This evaluation marks the first step in the development of an ingestible capsule for in-vivo analysis of intestinal gases.

articleTitle: Printed Piezoelectric Harvester for Integration in a Wearable Energy Storage Device
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Energy storage and harvesting technologies are intricately linked. Various technologies have been developed to convert environmental energies into electricity. For instance, piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) capture mechanical motion/vibration energy. Additionally, efforts have been directed towards integrating these energy harvesting devices into flexible/wearable units suitable for wearable electronics. This study showcases a printed flexible piezoelectric energy harvester with PVDF-TrFE and silver electrode, organized as a double-sided coating onto the polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate, thus forming the front side electrode for the PENG and backside electrode for a storage thin film element. A dielectric film of Al2O3 and the top electrode of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate)(PEDOT:PSS)/ graphene composite are applied by printing, realizing layer-by-layer assembly. The capabilities of the energy harvesting devices were characterized by a one-point eclipsed bending test, and the experimental results are presented to substantiate the potential utility of the fabricated device. This method provides a more controlled and uniform loading scenario for accurate testing without dependence on the sample length. It was found that loading of 100 g/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> produces a symmetric electrical signal with a magnitude of ~ ±0.4 V from a sample with an area of 2.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This voltage is sufficient to drive the charging of a sample supercapacitor, which will be investigated further.

articleTitle: Stretchable Strain Sensor using Interdigitated Capacitor on Fabric
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this paper, we present the development of a textile-based strain sensor aimed at creating a lightweight and portable device. The sensor is designed as an interdigitated capacitor, consisting of two electrodes fabricated from commercially available conductive material and adhered to an elastic non-conductive textile substrate. The elastic properties of the substrate enable the sensor to undergo stretching, thereby modifying its geometry (the separation between electrode fingers) and consequently influencing its electrical properties, specifically capacitance. Initial testing of the developed sensor involved three stretching positions, with the results confirming the effective functionality of the designed sensor. Moreover, suitable electronics, including a microcontroller for data acquisition, have been developed. The sensor was positioned on the elbow to assess its performance, particularly in monitoring arm flexion. The results have validated the consistent operation of the system.

articleTitle: 3-axis Accelerometer IMU in Various Degrees of Freedom Multi-switch Button Array
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The subject of the contribution is the analysis of the multimodal 3-axis accelerometer inertial unit in the sensing element function for a contactless switching component or its array. A linear model utilizing the dynamic acceleration and an 8-element inclination model utilizing the static acceleration were implemented. Incorporating an appropriate mechanical assembly, enables reliable recognition of individual states and resistance to interference and false detections. The purpose of the effort is to unfold the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) application potential in terms of its robustness, reliability, and applicability for a contactless switch array.

articleTitle: Development of Sensor Emulators for Testing the Safety Mechanisms of Sensor Interfaces in Automotive Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The test equipment used in automotive industry for evaluating the behavior of electric/electronic (E/E) system includes, in most of the cases, emulators of electrical car environment. The device under test (DUT) is an electronic module (that is, Electronic Control Unit – ECU) whose inputs and outputs are stimulated/loaded with the corresponding input signals from sensors or switches, and proper actuators. The most convenient way to cover all test requirements is to emulate all these inputs and outputs and control the signal parameters using a computerized system. By adding the vehicle simulation data in the control loop, the setup is called Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL). Considering the safety mechanisms implemented in safety critical systems in a vehicle, the test equipment can be adapted to directly address the safety requirements coverage and automatic test report generation, as described in ISO26262 Automotive Safety series of standards. This paper aims the development of sensor emulators, as part of a HiL system, in such a way that simplifies the hardware test setup and covers as much as possible all test cases defined for hardware integration of the DUT.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Lowpass Filter with an Ultra-wide Stopband using Triangular Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This research presents a compact Lowpass Filter (LPF) that employs triangular-shaped resonators to achieve an ultra-wide stopband and sharp response in the transmission band. An accurate LC equivalent model is computed for the basic resonator of this design. The proposed LPF features a -3 dB cut-off frequency of 2.2 GHz. Moreover, it provides an ultra-wide stopband extending from 2.9 GHz to 50 GHz, with attenuation levels above 20 dB. The compact dimensions of the LPF are 25.7 mm by 12.1 mm, which corresponds to 0.25 λg by 0.12 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> is the guided wavelength at 2.2 GHz. The proposed design employs the Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate, characterized by a 20 mil thickness and a relative dielectric constant of 2.2. The performance of the designed LPF is compared with several advanced filters to demonstrate its advantages. In upcoming studies, this LPF could be integrated into modern microwave communication systems to effectively suppress unwanted harmonics.

articleTitle: Increasing Productivity in Vapour Phase Soldering Using Vertical Stacking of Boards
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: During vapour phase soldering, the lateral size of the specimen tray determines the number of assemblies that can be soldered at once. Increased productivity, thus less power consumption can be achieved by increasing the size of the tray, and the workspace of the oven; therefore, also the size of the machine. This means significant additional costs both in terms of machine design and the amount of heat transfer fluid used. The aim of our research was to find out how we can increase the productivity of an industrial grade oven and improve the technology for a more energy efficient production, without making any significant retrofitting modifications. By stacking multiple printed circuit boards (PCB), we could increase the number of PCBs that could be soldered at once up to three times. We designed a sample holder with reduced mass, which shortened the cycle time. We performed comparative tests in several vertical configurations, compared to the default setup. We examined the resulting thermal profiles, performed shear tests, examined the surface of the cracks with optical microscopy, and also performed a cross section analysis. The results show that the solder joint quality was degraded due to increased void formation; however, the overall product quality might fit the requirements of commercial electronics.

articleTitle: The Effect of Oxide Reduction Using Formic Acid Vapours on The Thickness of The Conductive Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper deals with the effect of the formic acid vapours on the thickness and roughness of the conductive layer during oxide reduction process. To fully understand influence of the process is important for the main goal of the whole research, which is creation of high-quality connections by soldering while abandoning from conventional flux in the process. By not using the flux, cleaning and impurities issues can be fully avoided, thus increasing the quality and reducing the price of final products. Conductive layers thickness was analysed by laser confocal microscopy before and after controlled oxidation and afterward oxide reduction process. In the article are discussed several different scenarios that can occur when dealing with differently oxidized substrates, how to handle them, and the effect of differently setup cleaning profiles. Overall suitability of the usage of the formic acid vapours for cleaning of the oxidation of the copper conductive paths is stated.

articleTitle: Influence of Number of Turns on Common-Mode Choke’s Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper presents the characterization, simulation and modeling of common mode choke (CMC), intended to suppress electromagnetic interference. Since the knowledge of CMC characteristics is significant for the correct design of an electronic circuit to meet the electromagnetic compatibility standards, this paper presents the procedure of CMC characterizing by measuring scattering parameters (S-parameters) using a spectrum analyzer. The Open-Circuit method is used for the CMC’s electrical parameters extraction and investigating its efficiency in suppressing common-mode and differential-mode interference in the frequency range up to 50 MHz. The CMC is an inductive component comprising a commercially available toroid employed as a magnetic core and two windings of insulated wires wound around it. The ferrite material (its properties and geometry) and the windings determine CMC’s electrical characteristics (rated current, frequency range, characteristics impedance, and insertion loss). Therefore, the number of turns’ influence on its characteristics will be investigated to provide a fast design of CMC for a certain application.

articleTitle: A TeraRanger One Based LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this paper, a LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) device is proposed. The purpose was to create a low-cost, high-quality LiDAR, which can be used by robotics projects. It is based on the TeraRanger One distance measurement sensor, which can read distances up to 14 meters with a 1 KHz frequency. The sensor is rotated 360 degrees with a stepper motor and the distance to the surrounding objects is measured after each motor step. The device is controlled by an Arduino Nano board, which sends the readings through serial port.

articleTitle: Unlocking Insights: A Systematic Survey of Material Composition in Lithium-Ion Battery Cells for Recycling Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Battery recycling involves the recovery of materials from end-of-life (EOL) batteries, which are subsequently reused in the manufacturing of new products. Metals such as cobalt, lithium, nickel, manganese, aluminium, and copper are essential components of the electrodes of common lithium-ion batteries. In light of the growing demand for advancements in battery recycling, there is a critical need to start systematically documenting the chemistry of different types of batteries and to monitor the changes within their internal composition between the different states of charge, such as full charge, full discharge, deep discharge or shipping-state. In this work, a new methodology for a complex, quick, cheap, and effective material composition survey is presented. This methodology was applied to three types of cylindrical (18650) cells with two different cathode materials, specifically nickel cobalt aluminium (NCA) and nickel manganese cobalt (NMC), all with a capacity range from 3350 to 3500 mAh. This work offers a comprehensive, step-by-step description of the versatile battery research process, serving as the foundation for a streamlined and effective methodology for obtaining selected chemical and material parameters. The research endeavours to compare the material composition of lithium-ion cells at various states of charge to assess recycling potential and establish a database containing battery parameters. The results are essential for the automation and roboticization of the advanced recycling sector.

articleTitle: Active balancing using the DC2100B-C and DC2100B-D module
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The propulsion system is undoubtedly the most important component of an electric vehicle. It includes the electric motor, the battery, and the associated electronic control. In terms of cost, the battery accounts for approximately 50% of the initial vehicle cost. The battery is accompanied by a management system that performs various functions, including cell balancing. This work aims to present a monitoring and active balancing system for a set of 24 cells using Analog Devices' DC2100B-C and DC2100B-D modules, which implement a flyback converter balancing technique. The DC2100B Demonstration Circuit is designed as a Bidirectional Cell Balancer, employing two LTC®3300-1 ICs to actively balance up to 12 Li-Ion cells. It incorporates a single LTC6804-2 Multi-Cell Addressable Battery Stack Monitor IC for cell voltage measurement and utilizes two LTC3300-1 ICs for active cell balancing. Additionally, the DC2100B-C variant includes a PIC18F47J53 microcontroller. To highlight the balancing process, cells were randomly discharged to create an imbalance among them. Experimental results show that active balancing is successfully achieved, with cell voltages reaching the same level after the process. Furthermore, the experimental results align with theoretical concepts, and to demonstrate the functionality of the balancing stand, some simulations of the system were conducted using MATLAB Simulink and PSIM. Considering the substantial number of cells in a battery pack and the associated high costs, the balancing process remains a focal point of interest. Active balancing serves to prevent premature cell damage and can improve the overall efficiency of the pack. In this work, the key research and engineering aspects involve designing an equalizer based on a flyback transformer for a battery pack and validating the applicability of the equalizer during both discharge and charge processes to enhance the maximum discharge capacity and available capacity.

articleTitle: Laser powder bed fusion of titanium alloyed copper powder for power electronic substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Ceramics substrates are key components in high-power electronic modules like inverters for traction or energy applications. Since the state-of-the-art processes active metal brazing and direct copper bonding for the production of structured metallizations on ceramic substrates lack flexibility and require resource-intensive chemical and thermal treatments, an alternative metallization approach based on processing of a copper powder alloy with 2.6 wt.% titanium via laser powder bed fusion is presented in this paper. Within the presented study, the additively metallized ceramic substrates were analyzed via shear testing and cross sections to quantify adhesion and for assessment of the interface with regard to cracking mechanisms and porosity. With the presented powder alloy the formation of a reaction layer at the metal-ceramic-interface after laser fusion was detected via energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. In active metal brazing such reaction layers are a prerequisite for wetting of ceramic substrates with an active brazing alloy, which bonds an electrically functional copper layer to the ceramic substrate. Due to the observed formation of conchoidal fractures at the interface and the low electrical conductivity of copper-titanium alloys, an additive multi-material approach with a thin copper-titanium interlayer and an electrically functional copper layer is further presented.

articleTitle: Effect of Electro(less) Plating on Mechanical and Geometric Properties of Polymer-metal Structures Based on 3D Printed Models
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper deals with the study of the properties of polymer-metal structures, where polymer parts were made using additive 3D printing technologies. Thick metal layers were deposited on the surface of polymer parts by electro(less) deposition. The bending properties of the polymer-metal structures were characterized in comparison with the uncoated polymer parts. Based on the simulations and the results obtained, the development of new polymer-metal structures using thick film chemical plating was proceeded. In the experiment, an initial verification of the feasibility of thick film chemical plating was carried out at a thickness of 200 µm. The effect of the proposed process on the geometrical properties of the components is discussed using study models.

articleTitle: Electronic Nose Based on AI-capable Sensor Module for Beverages Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this paper, we present an electronic nose application case study based on an affordable Bosch BME688 AI (artificial intelligence) capable sensor module set (and development kit) to distinguish and identify different soft drinks and beverages. During the work, the device was prepared for TinyML and AI-based identification. The module contains eight pieces of BME688 sensors, and it is compatible with the Bosch BME AI Studio software. Based on their unique odor profiles, we created and tested various ML (machine learning) algorithms to distinguish between fruit palinka (fruit spirit) types, different beers, and ethanol. The case study aims to determine whether the module can distinguish between beverages. For this, we applied passive delivery. It was found that the differentiation between air and different samples (cola, lager beer) is possible. Still, ethanol and spirits with high alcohol content saturate the device, pointing to future dynamic sampling (active delivery).

articleTitle: State-of-Charge Estimation Based on Open-Circuit Voltage Model Considering Hysteresis
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) play a pivotal role in various sectors such as transportation, aerospace, and stationary systems. Accurate estimation of their state-of-charge (SOC) is crucial for efficient utilization within battery management systems. This work presents an enhanced SOC estimation method for LIBs, leveraging both open-circuit voltage (OCV) and hysteresis models. A co-estimation architecture employing two estimators is proposed, firstly focusing on battery model parameter estimation, and secondly utilizing pseudo-OCV instead of voltage measurements as output. This modification offers enhanced accuracy, reduced reliance on extensive laboratory testing, and improved robustness, especially in applications with rapid temperature fluctuations. The proposed method is evaluated through dynamic discharge profile tests across temperature levels ranging from 5 to 45 °C. Root-mean-square errors of SOC estimation for various temperatures were improved from the baseline approach (0.0185-0.0420) down to 0.0090-0.0280 in the proposed approach, showcasing the effectiveness of incorporating hysteresis models into SOC estimation.

articleTitle: Study of Thermal Loading of Ceramic Capacitors during Reflow Soldering
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Simulation studies were carried out using the computational fluid dynamics approach (CFD) provided by the ANSYS software framework. The goal of these studies was to make thermo-mechanical assessments of unsoldering MLCC components from a PCB. Various MLCC components were soldered on a standard board with a thickness of 1.6 mm. Soldering was performed in a batch reflow oven (LPKF ProtoFlow S). Disassembly was carried out using a Hakko FR811 soldering repair station. The paper shows the results of the CFD simulation in the combination with the thermo-mechanical simulations within the ANSYS software framework.

articleTitle: The Use of Scatter Plot Charts for the Study of Changes in the Electrical Parameters of Conductive Adhesive Joints
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: For adhesive conductive joints, the most frequently measured electrical parameters are the resistance of the joint, the non-linearity of the volt-ampere characteristic of the joint, and its 1/f noise. The work is focused on the question of whether it is possible, based on a scatter chart, to estimate the changes of one parameter under a certain type of climatic stress from the changes of the same parameter under another type of climatic stress, and also on the question of whether it is possible, based on a scatter plot, to estimate the changes of one of a parameter induced by one type of climatic stress from changes in another parameter induced by the same type of stress. It was found that the first question can be answered in the affirmative and the second in the negative. Strong correlations were found for both adhesives. For Adhesive #1, it was between the change in non-linearity of the volt-ampere characteristic in wet aging and combined wet-heat aging. Another significant correlation was found here between the change in non-linearity of the volt-ampere characteristic and the change in 1/f noise during wet aging. For adhesive #2, a strong correlation was found between the change of the resistance during the exposition of the joints in higher moisture and heat. Next strong correlation was also found between the resistance and non/linearity of the joint for aging in combined climate moisture-heat. Based on the mentioned correlations, it is possible to construct scatter plot charts which can be used to make especially long-term climate tests of conductive adhesives more efficient.

articleTitle: Investigation of In-Situ Polymerization in a Doped Methacrylate Resin
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this work, the in-situ polymerization of UDMA-TEGDMA (urethane-dimethacrylate – triethyleneglycol dimethacrylate) 3:1 polymer mixture was investigated. Our goal was to detect the change in the refractive index of UDMA:TEGDMA 3:1 during blue light-induced polymerization. The methacrylate resin mixture was doped with gold nanorods, and the change in the absorption band of these nanorods was monitored by spectrometer during the polymerization process. As the operation of the spectrometer and the received signal can be disturbed by the blue light lamp, an optical bandpass filter was used. From the collected data we were able to calculate the RI change during the photo-crosslinking and get a better understanding of the kinetics of the material.

articleTitle: Thermal Coupling of NTC Chip Thermistors
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: A novel device called thermal coupling of NTC chip thermistors was made by combining two electrically isolated chip thermistors Th<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and Th<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> having small dimensions (0603) and small power (1/10 W). The first thermistor Th<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> (input thermistor) is self-heating at a constant supply voltage U – it generates heat while the second thermistor Th<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is passive (output thermistor) – it receives heat. Thermistors are electrically insulated, but thermally coupled. The temperature dependence of NTC chip thermistors R(T) was measured and exponential factor of thermistor resistance B was determined. After that, current I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> of self–heating thermistor as a function of supply voltage U and using resistance R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> of input thermistor was determined. The electrical resistance of output thermistor R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> was measured by multimeter at the same time as the current of input thermistor. Using the Steinhart – Hart equation the temperature T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> of both thermistors were determined. The application of novel thermistor junction is expected in power microelectronics for electrical decoupling/thermal coupling of input to output slowly changeable signals.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties’ Stability of Flexible Carbon-Based Conductive Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper deals with the electrical properties’ stability of flexible carbon-based conductive layers by applying the bending tests (1 million cycles for every sample). The first part of experiments delves into the design, fabrication, and characterization of carbon-based conductive layers, exploring the influence of various shapes of conductive tracks. The second part of experiments are focused on detailed investigation of conductive joints realization between the SMD components (0R resistors with 0805 packages) by analyzing different layouts and three materials for the joint’s creation. For this reason, the carbon-based conductive glue, silver-filled epoxy conductive glue and low-temperature solder paste were used and analyzed. The final paper systematically evaluates the stability of electrical properties, including conductivity and resistance, under different mechanical deformations and stressors by applying the axial and radial bending tests. The stability of electrical properties demonstrated in this paper paves the way for the development of more resilient and durable electronic carbon-based structures, offering new possibilities for the integration of flexible electronics into everyday devices and emerging technologies.

articleTitle: Effect of New Types of PCB Surface Finishes on Fractographic Morphology of Solder Joints
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The aim of this paper was to study the fracture mechanisms of soldered joints after the shear test and to examine the interrelationships between the mechanical strength and the corresponding fracture morphologies. In our article, we compared 4 standard types of PCB surfaces (ENIG, ImSn, SnHASL, Cu) with 4 new developed type surface finishes based on SnAg. The smallest susceptibility to brittle failure and susceptibility to aging compared to other finishes was also demonstrated by the fractographic analysis of the fracture surfaces SnAg based surface. Overall, SnAg5 showed higher shear strength, greater pseudo-ductility and toughness than ENIG.

articleTitle: Silver Sintering Application in Packaging Al Metallized Chip onto Au Metallized Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This study investigates the application of Ag paste sintering technology in bonding Al metallized Si chips to Au metallized Cu sheet 1 mm thick substrates. The Al/Ag interface plays a crucial role in this connection. The research demonstrates that the mechanical characteristics of this interface are influenced by the roughness of the Al metallization, sintering conditions, and the presence of oxygen at the Al/Ag interface. The study achieved joints with adhesion strengths exceeding 10 MPa. Long-term annealing of samples at 200°C causes a significant decrease in adhesion to several MPa. The decrease in adhesion is a result of thermal stresses generated by high temperature and significant differences in the TCE of the Si chip and Cu substrate, as well as the increased mobility of Ag atoms. This translates into a reduction in the effective bonding surface area and thus a decrease in adhesion.

articleTitle: Thermal Diffusivity Determination of a Semiconductor Device
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The heat transfer through semiconductor power devices stands for a main factor of limitation for their operation. Power semiconductor devices are usually assembled in multilayer structures together with their cooling circuits. To optimize the thermal management of these power structures, this study approaches the transient operation of the power semiconductor devices. Transient operation of the power semiconductor devices can produce thermal accumulation of heat, producing faults in operation. A key thermal parameter in transient operation of power semiconductor devices is thermal diffusivity. In this paper is presented a new method of measurement of the thermal diffusivity of multilayer electronic structures together with their cooling circuits. The method presented is investigating the transient state of the operating power semiconductor devices using three distinct kinds of temperature sensors. The method is using a periodical heat wave and real time data from digital temperature sensors to measure the thermal diffusivity of a power electronic system.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of a Two-Stage Grid-Connected MPPT Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Nowadays, roof-top PC installations are gaining increasing popularity. Grid-connected inverters with maximum power point tracking (MPPT) capability are used to interface the PV panel with the power grids. High-efficiency requirements and environmental pollution concerns enabled the development of various single-phase two-stage grid-connected inverters. Usually, the first stage is a boost converter with maximum power point tracking and the second stage is the inverter that enables the connection to the grid. This paper proposes a single-phase grid-connected MPPT inverter. It offers a complete design methodology for the interleaved boost converter oriented towards its specific operation as a step-up converter with MPPT. It also proposes an average simulation model for the complete PV system that improves simulation times considering that these types of systems are complex and are difficult to simulate as a whole.

articleTitle: Development an Ultra-Low Power "Coin" Size Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this paper is presented a real prototype of ultra-low power battery powered sensor board which is aimed to be the "coin" size device. Prototype squeeze in small size MCU + radio module + sensor capable of measuring temperature, humidity and atmospheric pressure. The realization from schematic to prototype production is described in the article.

articleTitle: Variations in Open Circuit Voltage of Cycle-Aged Lithium-Ion Batteries due to Silicon-Enhanced Anodes
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: We present the outcomes of cycle aging tests performed on 16 lithium-ion battery cells of different types, both commercially available: INR21700M50LT produced by LG Energy Solution and INR18650M35A produced by Molicel. These cells exhibit differences in silicon content within the anode, coupled with the utilization of two different cathode materials. Throughout the testing process, the cells underwent cycling with different state of charge (SOC) windows: 0-90%, 0-30%, 30-60% and 60-90% as well as routine checkup phases, which include a measurement of the residual capacity and of the quasi-open circuit voltage (qOCV) curve. After 260 equivalent full cycles, we found substantial differences in the aging of the two cell types, evident in both their state of health and in the variations of the qOCV curve. The LG M50LT displayed a notably slower capacity fade up to 3x less with respect to the Molicel M35A under identical testing conditions. We also found out that cycling in the SOC window 0-90% produced the least pronounced variations in the qOCV curve of the LG M50LT, while the opposite is true for the Molicel M35A. This discrepancy cannot be explained only in terms of a different silicon content, therefore the reasons have to be searched in the complex interactions between the two anode materials, as well as in cathode material degradation.

articleTitle: Design of a Flat Coil Electrothermal Vaporization Device for Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometry
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This article presents an analysis on developing an innovative filament design for the electrothermal evaporation process. This new concept enhances stability and repeatability, thereby improving measurement precision in multi-element analysis using atomic spectrometry. This study details various constructive solutions that have been implemented, providing an in-depth analysis of the results obtained, as well as an evaluation of their advantages and disadvantages in relation to the multi-elemental analysis process. This evaluation is conducted using COMSOL Multiphysics, a tool dedicated to finite element simulations suited to these types of analysis. Additionally, the research explores the possibility of supplying power to the filament in a controlled manner using a laboratory power supply together with different optimization methods for the evaporation process, implemented in LabView.

articleTitle: Intra-Day Optimal Dispatching of an Islanded Microgrid under Solar Power Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage optimization strategy for an islanded microgrid, using day-ahead dispatching and an intra-day optimization stage, implemented as a rolling window optimization. The day-ahead dispatching is executed once every 24 hours to obtain the optimal scheduling plan of the units, for the whole day, considering the minimum operating cost of the microgrid. The intra-day optimization runs every hour to adjust the output of the units, according to newer short-term solar predictions, and to ensure that the functioning of the battery energy storage system remains within the predefined operating envelope A clear day, from 3 different seasons, is used for testing, ensuring that a wide range of scenarios is covered. The performance of the proposed two-stage optimization strategy is determined by comparing it against the single stage approach, where the solar variations are covered solely by the batteries. Significant economic gains were obtained in 2 out of the 3 scenarios while the battery energy storage system remained within the defined operating envelope, compared to the single stage approach, in all the 3 cases.

articleTitle: Propagation Delay Analysis by Employing Various PCB Manufacturing Process
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: With the continuous increase in the data rate of high-performance memory modules, signal propagation delay has become a dominant factor in determining system performance, such as timing margin. As propagation delay is determined mainly by the dielectric constant of the material and PCB processes, it is of utmost importance to control the type of dielectric material and fabrication process used in production. However, different PCB vendors adopt different materials and processes, resulting in timing mismatching among vendors. In this paper, we investigate the factors leading to signal timing mismatch, and propose methods to control the timing difference caused by various manufacturing environment and material properties.

articleTitle: Thick-Film CuNi-Ag and CuNi-Cu Thermocouples and Thermoelectric Microgenerators
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Electrical and thermoelectric properties of thickfilm planar thermoelectric microgenerators made on the basis of constantan-, copper- and silver-based inks are investigated and analyzed in a wide temperature range from 250 to 400 K. The Seebeck coefficient for both systems, CuNi-Ag and CuNiCu, has similar values and increases as a function of temperature. This parameter is about 3-5 µV/K higher than the Seebeck coefficient value for a T-type wire thermocouple (copper-constantan).

articleTitle: Detection of Nucleotides Using Gold Nanoprisms Immobilized on Glass
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Gold nanoparticles have a wide range of application areas, including drugdelivery systems, catalysts, and biosensors. Our long-term aim is to create biosensors from gold nanoparticles based on localized surface plasmon resonance. In order to achieve this objective, the immobilization of the nanoprisms on a solid surface (e.g. glass) is of paramount importance. Different methods were tested to obtain reproducible results. This work presents the experiments regarding the immobilization of the synthetized particles and the successful binding of nucleotides to the nanoprisms. The nucleotides were detected using Raman-spectroscopy.

articleTitle: NTC Thermistor Ferrite Composite for Temperature Sensing with Reduced Humidity Influence
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Negative temperature coefficient (NTC) thermistors, made from semiconducting oxides such as ferrites and used as resistance-based temperature sensors, remain a focus of research, as they are fundamental building blocks of many electronic systems. In this work NTC thermistor properties of a ferrite composite (MnFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) ceramics obtained by solid-state sintering in the form of a bulk sample were investigated. Bulk samples in the form of pellets had an average diameter of 8.7 mm and thickness of 1.8 mm. A thermal (material) constant (B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10,90</inf>) of 4390 K calculated from measured impedance at 100 Hz in the temperature range 10 - 90 °C and temperature sensitivity of -4.87 %/K at 25 °C was obtained. These values fall within the range required for a commercial NTC thermistor material (B between 2000 and 5000, temperature sensitivity between -2 and 6% K at room temperature -25 °C). The influence of relative humidity (RH) change in the range 30-90% at the temperatures of 25 and 50 °C on impedance was monitored within the frequency range 50 Hz – 1 MHz. The obtained results showed that at 100 Hz impedance reduced from 8.15 to 3.56 MOhm at 25 °C and from 2.81 to 1.65 MOhm at 50 deg C for RH from 30 to 90%.The results indicate that the impact of humidity on impedance was less pronounced compared to the effect of temperature on impedance. Future work will focus on applying this ferrite composite in flexible printed temperature sensors.

articleTitle: The use of bending experiments for the efficient characterization of the mechanical functionality of component interconnections
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The formation of cracks in both electrical components and their interconnections is a huge problem in the use of electronic devices because they typically result in a total failure of the system. In order to minimize resulting repair or replacement costs, an accurate understanding of the crack formation process is necessary, e.g. with the help of suitable experiments. One possibility would be the use of temperature cycling tests, but such tests involve long periods of time lasting several months and cause high costs. Another option that has not yet established in this context is the use of bending experiments which can be conducted in a much shorter time. This paper presents the results of four-point bending tests on MLCC (multilayer ceramic capacitor) and QFN (quad flat no leads package) components to discuss their ability to evaluate the robustness of components and solder interconnects. Subsequent FEM (finite element method) simulations were carried out in order to account for true strains and stresses that occur during the test in the solder interconnects of the components.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band Wilkinson Power Divider Using Compact Lowpass Filter with Wide Suppression Band
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-band Wilkinson Power Divider (WPD) utilizing a compact Lowpass Filter (LPF) with a wide suppression band. The proposed divider demonstrates excellent performance at operating frequencies of 0.9 GHz and 2.7 GHz, along with effective harmonic suppression in the range of 4.8 GHz to 11.8 GHz. Moreover, the proposed design achieves over a 50% size reduction compared to conventional WPDs. This harmonic suppression and size reduction are achieved by integrating two LPFs into the WPD branches in place of the traditional λ/4 transmission lines. The proposed lowpass filter has a 3.1 GHz cut-off frequency and provides a stopband from 4.8 GHz to 10 GHz. The harmonic suppression range provided by the LPFs ensures that unwanted signals are effectively attenuated. The suggested design is particularly suitable for GSM communication systems, while size constraints and harmonic interference are critical considerations.

articleTitle: Portable Device for In-Situ Cyclic Voltammetry Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Development of devices for in-situ cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements attracted huge interest in the scientific community in the past years. However, most of the reported solutions require the connection to the smartphone or PC-based unit for data storage, interpretation, and presentation. Consequently, the possibility for automated and unsupervised electrochemical measurements is limited. Advancing the state of the art, in this paper we present a portable device for in-situ scan rate configuration, CV measurements and CV curve plotting. The device is battery-powered, equipped with a color display, SD card for data storage, and an embedded keypad for device configuration. The range of output voltage range is ±1 V (8-bits resolution), while the current range is ±200 μA (10-bits resolution). Seven values of scan rate from 10 mV/s to 300 mV/s are selectable. Comparative analysis with Palmsens4 device revealed high similarity in measured values with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=0.99. Finally, actual CV curves measured on an electrochemical system (screen printed three-electrode cell and a 10 ml solution of 0.5 mM Sodium ferri/ferro cyanide and 0.1 M Sodium Chloride) are presented.

articleTitle: Design of a Quadrature Hybrid Coupler with Triple Tapered Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to designing a Quadrature Hybrid Coupler (QHC) utilizing Triple Tapered Resonators (TTR) to achieve harmonic suppression. In this case, triple-tapered resonators are effectively integrated into the horizontal and vertical main branches of the conventional coupler, leading to modifying the structure of the main branches. The triple-tapered resonators play a crucial role in suppressing harmonics and enhancing the coupler performance. The presented QHC operates at 2 GHz frequency with a bandwidth of 230 MHz and effectively can suppress 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>, 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup>, 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>, and 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonics. The outcomes of this research highlight the effectiveness of triple-tapered resonators in achieving successful harmonics suppression. The presented design offers promising features for application in efficient communication systems, where harmonic interference is a critical consideration.

articleTitle: Modelling the Effect of Laser-Trimming on the Electrical Properties of Thick-film Resistors
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this paper, various thick-film resistor trimming geometries and their effects on resistor properties, including resistance value, current density distribution and perceived inhomogeneity of power density within the functional layer. Experimental EDAG 6017 SS polymer paste resistors were stencil printed on an FR4 substrate using immersion silver plated ISO 162525-2 compliant measuring pattern and cured at datasheet recommended parameters. Resistance values were measured with a DC 4-wire method, and the trims were cut using a frequency tripled Nd:YAG UVA laser; they were measured again at each step. The topology of the experimental resistor samples was recorded using an Olympus DSX100 motorised stage measuring microscope using the focus stacking method. This resulted in height (thickness) information at a fine resolution. The thickness data was used to build a 3D model geometry for finite element method (FEM) simulation of untrimmed and trimmed resistors. The prepared geometry was procedurally trimmed using the same length and spot size parameters as the laser micromachining. The various geometries' stationary current behaviour was FEM simulated using MATLAB PDEtool, and properties were determined by post-processing of nodal results. A comparison of measured and numerically approximated resistance values proves sufficient predictive power at the current abstraction level.

articleTitle: FCCSP Warpage Scope Evaluation for 5G Product with Advanced Wafer Node
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: 5G is the fifth-generation mobile communication network. The upgrade of each generation of communication technology brings revolutionary changes to terminal products and drives the reconstruction and great changes of the entire industrial chain. 5G applications are not simply to provide a smoother network than 4G, but to completely change people’s work and lifestyles from all walks of life and social operations, so it is widely used. In order to meet the market’s requirements for 5G features with high power and high performance, chip performance from the past has been improved by improvements in semiconductor manufacturing processes. Therefore, chip wafer node reduced is necessary for high performance product. For low wafer node technology accompanied by reducing die size. The substrate vendor’s fine layout capability is not able to reach the chip process, so small die size and large package size is a trend for further low wafer node product.For large package and small die size, it means large compound volume. Therefore, the microelectronics products of Flip Chip-Chip Scale Package (FCCSP) with more increasing challenges are faced to meet warpage criteria. In this paper, to predict FCCSP warpage scope for different die size to package size ratio and provide a guide to meet warpage criteria ensure package mount on PCB will not have risk. This warpage scope is produced from ANSYS software which can apply warpage simulation. We evaluate package size from 10mm to 18mm, and collocation different die ratio design. Then obtain room temp and high temp limit within warpage spec, if under this scope the warpage risk is low.From this study, we can conclude some results for die to package ratio design and we provide some solutions if out of this die to package ratio scope, for example change die thickness or change compound type to meet warpage criteria. In addition, we verify experiment data to check this ratio is appropriate or not. Finally, this simulation results are aligned with experiments and it can be used to predict.

articleTitle: Modelling of Battery Management System based on Switching Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this paper, a simulation model of a voltage balancing system for series connected cells of a supercapacitor battery is made. The Battery Management System (BMS) is based on switched capacitors used to actively balance the series connected cells of the battery. The semiconductor switch losses were investigated using the model. Based on the analysis of switching transients and energy transfer between individual cells, element selection requirements for these switches are defined. Typical waveforms for the currents and voltages are presented to define the requirements for the semiconductor structures. The simulation model has been developed with PLECS software. The losses in the transistor switches are investigated for several BMS operating modes.

articleTitle: Iron Nanoparticle-Doped Flux: Wetting Characteristics of Flux and SAC305 Solder and Effects on Flux Viscosity
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this study the influence of iron nanoparticles (Fe-NPs) on the wetting properties of soldering flux and solder as well as on the viscosity of the flux was investigated. Iron nanoparticles in varying concentrations from 0 to 10 wt.% were incorporated into the soldering flux. To quantify the viscosity changes, a rotational viscometer was employed, progressively increasing the shear rates during the measurements. The wetting behavior of the nanoparticle-enhanced flux was evaluated by using the drop sessile method. Furthermore, the study examined the impact of Fe-NPs on the wetting dynamics in the soldering process, utilizing SAC305 alloy as the solder medium. This research indicates that as the concentration of iron nanoparticles in the flux increases, there is a notable increase in the wetting angle of the SAC305 solder. Conversely, the flux itself exhibited enhanced wetting characteristics with the addition of nanoparticles. This observed decrease in the wetting angle of the flux, which correlates with the viscosity data, suggests that the integration of Fe-NPs contributes to a reduction in the flux’s viscosity.

articleTitle: Occurrence of Voids in Soldered Joints for Electrical Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The research focuses on the occurrence of voids in soldered joints in the field of electrical engineering. The main goal was to analyze the occurrence of voids in soldered joints and to propose effective strategies to minimize this defect. BGA chips mounted on 10-layer PCBs were chosen as test samples. The current work focuses on defining production conditions and analyzing X-ray images. The analysis results implies that the parameters were chosen correctly and the acceptability criteria according to the ECSS-Q-ST-70-61C standard (defining soldering qualification for the space industry) were met with a margin, allowing for further types of tests such as vibration test and temperature cycling.

articleTitle: Thick-Film Thermoelectric Structures Based on Ca3Co4O9 Thermopiles
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Electrical and thermoelectric properties of thickfilm planar thermoelectric devices based on calcium cobaltite (Ca<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> – Ca349) and silver-based inks are investigated and analyzed in a wide temperature range from 250 to 400 K. The The Seebeck coefficient for the Ca349-Ag system has value of about 140 µV/K and slightly decreases as a function of temperature. The tested thermocouples/thermopiles can be used as sensors of physical quantities.

articleTitle: Development of Computationally Efficient Numerical Models for Assessing the Reliability of Electronic Components under Vibration Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper focuses on developing efficient models based on the Finite Element Method for data synthesis that is useful for solder joint reliability predictions under vibration tests. Starting from an existing detailed 3D Finite Element model of a vibration test vehicle assembled with Flip Chip components, efficiency optimized models were generated. Models were simplified to make use of periodically present structures. The equivalent inelastic strain occurring in the corner solder joints of the Flip Chip components was extracted from the simulation results and was further evaluated to assess the simulation accuracy. While cutting the calculation time down to 9 minutes, the modifications introduced strain result deviations that however did not exceed 15%. Replacing volume elements in thin structures with shell elements helped to significantly reduce the number of elements and nodes, thus shortening the calculation time. Additionally, implementing a submodeling approach did significantly reduce the calculation time, too.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Electronics: Unveiling the Nexus of Circular Economy, Global Policies and Industry Impacts
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive literature review on sustainability in electronics technology. The paper focuses on three key areas - 1) a comparison of global sustainability policies and initiatives (for example - the EU Green Deal, Paris Agreement, the concept of Industry, 2) the circular economy, and 3) an assessment of barriers and potential benefits to industry based on the findings. As a practical contribution, the paper also includes an evaluation of a questionnaire survey conducted in cooperation with 22 companies from the electronics manufacturing sector, which focused on the implementation of measures related to the requirements of the EU Green Deal and the Industry 4.0 concept. The results of the survey show that most of the companies surveyed are not yet dealing with this issue, mainly for financial reasons.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Electronic Encryption System Based on Programmable Cellular Automata Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In recent years, in the field of digital electronics, technology opportunities creating many innovative openings for the implementation of increasingly complex encryption systems for data communication applications. One of the important issues is that our society could not maintain its real time current operations without protocols based on cryptography. On the basis of a systemic approach, we propose in this work a Programmable Cellular Automata (PCA) based cryptosystem which is able to efficiently secure data sent over the telecommunication networks. The reason for choosing a bio-inspired technique based on PCA to develop the security technology is due to their excellent performance including: massive parallelism, robustness, simplicity and relative ease of implementation in hardware solutions (e.g., Raspberry Pi or reconfigurable FPGA).

articleTitle: Realization of Cost-Effective Supercapacitors Utilizing Substitutable Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 47th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In today’s context, the growing concern revolves around developing reliable power systems that are both cost-effective and environmentally friendly. Research efforts increasingly focus on the development of supercapacitors, a component with numerous benefits in terms of lifespan, stored electrical energy capacity, and rapid charging compared to other means of storing electrical energy. Supercapacitors store more energy than regular capacitors, creating a very thin double layer of charge between two electrodes, which are made of porous materials, typically based on carbon. The electrodes effectively have a larger surface area and a smaller separation distance, which gives a supercapacitor the ability to store much more charge. In a supercapacitor, there is no dielectric. Instead, both electrodes are soaked in an electrolyte and separated by a very thin insulator.
